title: Monsoon and Wreck
premise: Wren Yarrow, a desert ranger who owes a life-debt to the smuggler who once saved them, is chasing a thief who stole their compass—the only relic of the family Wren can't remember. The trail leads to a tidal cave on a drowned coast, where the thief, a girl named Sefa, reveals the compass points not north but toward the source of the river that feeds the desert: a spring the river-cities have sealed and lied about for a century. Hunted by the smugglers' guild, who want the spring's location to control the water trade, Wren and Sefa travel upstream through drowned towns and memory-haunted ruins, discovering Wren's forgotten childhood at the spring's edge. At the source, Wren must choose between paying the debt by handing the spring to the guild or exposing the truth and losing the only belonging they've ever had; they choose truth, the spring opens, and Wren—compass finally pointing home—finds a new family not in the past but in the person beside them.
about_author: Mirabel Sterling is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons mapping seasonal waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who belong to landscapes more than to each other.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tracking a thief across the Ashen Flats, Wren rations water and memory in equal measure, revealing the debt they owe the smuggler Corvane and the compass stolen from their pack. The chapter establishes Wren's self-imposed invisibility and ends when the thief's trail turns, impossibly, toward the coast.

chapters.title: Where the Desert Ends
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reaches the drowned coast for the first time, unnerved by the tide's rhythm and the fishing villages that watch them pass without welcome. They learn the thief bought passage to the sea caves. A village elder warns: 'The caves only open for people the water remembers.' Wren doesn't know what that means yet.

chapters.title: The Cave That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At low tide, a cave mouth opens in the cliff, exactly as the legends describe. Inside, Wren finds the thief—Sefa—waiting, having left the compass deliberately on a stone altar. Sefa claims she didn't steal it; she borrowed it, because it's the only thing that points to the sealed spring. First confrontation, uneasy truce.

chapters.title: North Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa explains her history: raised by the river-cities' archivists, she discovered the compass is a spring-key, one of three, and the guild has been hunting the others. She shows Wren a map of the river's forbidden upper reaches. Wren refuses to believe it—until the compass needle swings toward the mountains, ignoring north entirely.

chapters.title: Corvane's Shadow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Guild riders arrive at the coast hunting them both; Wren recognizes the lead rider as one of Corvane's, sent to collect the debt in person. Wren and Sefa flee inland along the riverbank, and Wren realizes Corvane saved their life years ago for exactly this purpose: to use them as a key. Betrayal reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In a half-drowned river town, an old ferryman trades them passage for a story. He recognizes Wren's face and calls them by a name Wren doesn't remember: 'the spring-child.' He gives them a water-stained ledger with Wren's family name in it. Wren's amnesia begins to look less like accident, more like design.

chapters.title: Drowned Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pair dive a submerged village to retrieve the second compass-key from a church tower. Underwater sequence: bells, fish, and a flash of memory—Wren drowning as a child, someone pulling them out. Sefa saves Wren this time. The debt theme inverts: now Wren owes Sefa.

chapters.title: What the Guild Wants
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Captured briefly by a guild patrol, Sefa bargains her way free by lying about the spring's location, and we learn the guild's plan: control the spring, control the desert, end the river-cities' independence. Sefa realizes she's been used as bait to draw out the third key-holder. She suspects it's Wren.

chapters.title: The Memory Market
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A traveling bazaar sells bottled memories. Wren, desperate, buys a vial said to contain their own past—and experiences a fragment: their mother sealing the spring, their father handing them to strangers, 'keep her invisible.' The truth costs more than coin. Sefa watches Wren grieve a family they're only now meeting.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The river narrows into unmapped rapids; a rafting sequence where Sefa's river-craft and Wren's desert instincts finally complement each other. They save each other twice. Around the campfire after, Sefa admits she chose Wren not by chance—she's been following the compass's pull too, and it points at people, not places.

chapters.title: The First Lie
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Sefa hid a guild message offering amnesty if she delivers the key-holder. Confrontation in the rain. Sefa never intended to accept it, but the secrecy wounds Wren, who has built their whole life on being lied to. The partnership fractures; Wren walks on alone.

chapters.title: Alone Upstream
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Solo chapters of the gorge: Wren faces the river's guardians—territorial herons, a collapsing trail, and the growing pull of memories that sharpen with every mile. They realize the spring doesn't just feed the desert; it feeds memory, and the guild's sealing of it is why Wren forgot.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Alone, Sefa doubles back and confronts the guild patrol herself, feeding them a false route to buy Wren time. She's caught by Corvane, who is more charming and more terrifying than legend. He offers her the one thing she wants—recognition as an archivist—for the spring's true gate. She stalls, buying hours with her life.

chapters.title: The Gate of Roots
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reaches the sealed gate: living roots grown over stone, marked with their family's sigil. The compass dissolves in their hands, its metal becoming water. The gate opens only to a spring-child's blood. Wren enters the source cavern—and hears, echoing up from below, Sefa's voice in Corvane's custody.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside, the spring: a pool of light where memory lives as water. Wren drinks and remembers everything—their parents' sacrifice, the guild's century-old theft of the water, why they were hidden. Full restoration of the past, and the crushing realization that restoring the spring will destroy the desert settlements that have adapted to scarcity.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Corvane drags Sefa to the gate, using her as a hostage to make Wren open it. Sefa, refusing to be leverage, tells Corvane the gate kills liars—buying a moment—and shouts to Wren that the guild already poisoned the outflow years ago. The truth Wren must tell isn't just the spring's; it's the desert's.

chapters.title: Debt Collected
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane demands the debt: Wren's life, owed since the day he pulled them from a river. Wren offers it—kneels, blade at throat—and Corvane hesitates, because a dead key-holder opens nothing. Wren turns the debt into a trap: the spring judges intent, and Corvane's greed is laid bare as the water rises against him.

chapters.title: The Flood of Remembering
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: the spring, unsealed, floods the cavern with memory-water. Corvane, drowning in his own worst recollections, is spared only because Sefa pulls him out—mercy as the final argument against the guild's creed. The three compasses' power disperses into the river, and the gate closes forever behind them.

chapters.title: What the Water Carried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Downstream, the river runs clearer; villages wake to water that restores small memories—a song, a face. Wren must publicly tell the truth about the guild's poisoning and their own hidden identity, risking the desert's anger. Some forgive; some don't. Belonging, Wren learns, is offered, not owed.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Oath
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa declines Corvane's offer and instead founds a free archive at the river-cities, recording everything the guild buried—including Wren's family's story, told with their blessing. She and Wren formalize their partnership: not debt, not obligation, but chosen. The theme of loyalty vs. truth resolves: they serve truth together.

chapters.title: Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to the Ashen Flats as a ranger no longer hiding, the new compass—a gift from Sefa, pointing wherever Wren decides—on their belt. They visit their parents' grave at the spring's edge and finally say goodbye. The desert and the river are no longer separate countries in Wren's heart.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. A year later, the first true monsoon in a generation breaks over the desert. Wren and Sefa stand on a ridge watching rain fill the flats, and Wren—once invisible, once memoryless—is known by name in every village the water touches. The last line: the river remembers, and so do they.
